objective: Routing that minimizes transfer cost: VPC endpoints, VPC peering, AWS Transit Gateway, cross-AZ and cross-Region traffic
secondaryObjectives: NAT gateway cost: one shared gateway versus one per Availability Zone
Cost visibility: AWS Cost Explorer, AWS Budgets, the AWS Cost and Usage Report, cost allocation tags, multi-account billing
Designing out single points of failure

sources.cite: AWS. Amazon VPC pricing (NAT gateway pricing examples)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-11: the worked example for US East (Ohio) gives 'the rate is $0.045 per hour' and a data processing charge of $0.045 per GB; 'There are no data processing or hourly charges for using Gateway Type VPC endpoints'; the page suggests a gateway endpoint for S3 'To avoid the NAT Gateway Data Processing charge'. The scenario is placed in us-east-2 (Ohio) so these are the rates read. Prices change; re-check at the next review.

sources.cite: AWS. Amazon VPC User Guide: Pricing for NAT gateways
sources.note: Read 2026-11-11: charged 'for each hour that your NAT gateway is available and each gigabyte of data that it processes'; if most traffic is to AWS services that support gateway or interface endpoints, 'consider creating an interface endpoint or gateway endpoint for these services'.

sources.cite: AWS. Amazon VPC User Guide: NAT gateway basics
sources.note: Read 2026-11-11: 'Each NAT gateway is created in a specific Availability Zone and implemented with redundancy in that zone.' 'If you have resources in multiple Availability Zones and they share one NAT gateway, and if the NAT gateway's Availability Zone is down, resources in the other Availability Zones lose internet access.' 'To improve resiliency, create a NAT gateway in each Availability Zone, and configure your routing to ensure that resources use the NAT gateway in the same Availability Zone.'

sources.cite: AWS. AWS PrivateLink Guide: Gateway endpoints
sources.note: Read 2026-11-11: gateway endpoints serve Amazon S3 and DynamoDB 'without requiring an internet gateway or a NAT device'; 'There is no additional charge for using gateway endpoints'; the route is added to the route tables you select, and 'Instances in subnets that aren't associated with these route tables use the public service endpoint'; traffic to the service 'in a different Region goes to the internet gateway because prefix lists are specific to a Region'.

sources.cite: AWS. Cost Management User Guide: AWS Cost Anomaly Detection
sources.note: Read 2026-11-11: uses machine learning models 'to detect and alert on anomalous spend patterns'; alerts by email or an Amazon SNS topic; runs 'approximately three times a day' after billing data is processed; can take up to 24 hours to detect because it uses Cost Explorer data with a delay of up to 24 hours.

brief.situation: Monday 09:00. You run the platform for a photo-sharing app in us-east-2 (Ohio). Finance forwards last month's bill: about $2,900 under NAT Gateway, against a network budget of $800. Nothing in the architecture changed last month, but the new image pipeline went live.
handover: Two Availability Zones. App servers in an Auto Scaling group across private subnets in AZ a and AZ b; one NAT gateway in each public subnet; each private subnet's route table sends 0.0.0.0/0 to its own AZ's NAT gateway.
The app reads and writes images in an S3 bucket in us-east-2, copies a nightly backup to a bucket in us-west-2, and calls a card processor on the internet at checkout.
Checkout must stay up: the target is 99.9% a month.
howItWorks: Learner-paced: nothing moves until you act. Investigate, change the network, then run the week and see the bill and the events.
Changes show on the board; the meters show the projected NAT bill and checkout availability.
Before you run the week you are asked to write what is driving the bill and what you will change. The debrief scores what you did.

backupQ.title: The backup copy
backupQ.context: Does the new gateway endpoint also carry the nightly backup copy to the bucket in us-west-2?

choices.label: No: a gateway endpoint serves S3 in this Region only; the backup still leaves through NAT
choices.feedback: Right. The endpoint's prefix list is for us-east-2; cross-Region S3 traffic still goes out through the NAT gateway (about $90 a month here).

choices.label: Yes: all S3 traffic now uses the endpoint
choices.feedback: No. Gateway endpoints route only to the service in the current Region; traffic to S3 in another Region goes out the normal way, here through the NAT gateway.

then.log: Tuesday: NAT data processing for the day is running at about {round(procGb / 30)} GB, {round(natCost / 30)|usd} a day.
Thursday 14:00: AWS Health reports impaired connectivity in us-east-2a for 90 minutes. The load balancer shifts traffic to AZ b.
AZ b's instances send their internet traffic through NAT gateway A in the impaired AZ: card-processor calls fail. Checkout is down for 90 minutes.
Checkout fails for 90 minutes: the remaining NAT gateway's AZ is the only path, and routing is broken.
AZ b has its own NAT gateway: checkout keeps working on the AZ b instances.
Sunday: the cost monitors are in place, so a spike like last month's would raise an alert within about a day.

else.log: Sunday: no cost alert is configured; the next surprise would again arrive with the monthly bill.

plan.question: Before you run the week: what is driving the bill, what did you change, and what did you make sure not to break?

parts.label: The cause and the fix
parts.criteria: Names NAT gateway data processing (not hours) as the driver, from same-Region S3 traffic of the image pipeline; fixes it with an S3 gateway endpoint (no hourly or data charge) on every private route table; notes the cross-Region backup still goes through NAT.
parts.modelAnswer: Almost all of it is NAT data processing at $0.045 per GB for about 60 TB of S3 traffic to a bucket in the same Region. An S3 gateway endpoint on both private route tables takes that traffic off the NAT gateways at no charge. The backup to us-west-2 still goes through NAT, because a gateway endpoint only serves S3 in its own Region.

parts.label: What not to break
parts.criteria: Keeps one NAT gateway per AZ for internet-bound traffic (the card processor) so losing one AZ does not cut the other off; does not delete the NAT gateways; adds cost visibility (Budgets alert, Cost Anomaly Detection) so the next spike is caught in a day.
parts.modelAnswer: Keep a NAT gateway in each AZ: the card-processor calls still need the internet, and with one shared gateway an AZ failure cuts off the other AZ. Saving $33 a month is not worth that. Add a budget alert and an anomaly monitor so a spike shows up within a day, not on the bill.

expertPath.text: Cost Explorer by usage type: NAT data processing, not hours. Flow logs: 60 TB of same-Region S3 traffic, 2 TB to the us-west-2 backup, 0.5 TB to the card processor.
One change: an S3 gateway endpoint on both private route tables. The backup copy to us-west-2 still uses NAT. Keep both NAT gateways for the card-processor calls.
A budget alert and a Cost Anomaly Detection monitor. Run the week: about $180 a month projected, and checkout survives Thursday's AZ impairment.

outage.headline: Checkout outage
outage.body: The NAT bill was data processing, which the gateway endpoint removes for free. Deleting NAT gateways saved little and took away the internet path the card processor needs, or the AZ independence that survives an AZ failure.

fixed.headline: Fixed without breaking anything
fixed.body: You confirmed the cause with data, made the one change that removes it, kept a NAT gateway per AZ and added monitoring. That is the expert path.

partly.headline: Better, by a rougher route
partly.body: Check whether you looked at the data before changing things, whether both route tables got the endpoint, and whether each AZ kept its own NAT gateway.

time_up.headline: No decision
time_up.body: The bill keeps growing while nothing changes.

scoring.modelReasoning: A NAT gateway bill is hours plus data processed. Here the hours are about $66 a month for two gateways; the rest is $0.045 per GB of data processing, nearly all from the image pipeline talking to an S3 bucket in the same Region. A gateway endpoint for S3 carries that traffic with no hourly or data charge, but only for the route tables it is associated with and only to S3 in the same Region, so it goes on both private route tables and the cross-Region backup still uses NAT. Internet-bound traffic (the card processor) still needs NAT, and one NAT gateway per AZ keeps each AZ independent: with one shared gateway an AZ failure cuts the other AZ off. Confirm the cause in Cost Explorer and flow logs before changing anything, and add a budget alert and Cost Anomaly Detection so the next spike is caught within a day.
